[Start state] In a community-centre room with a wood floor, a blank cork board on the wall and cool fluorescent light mixed with window light from the LEFT side of the image frame, six grey folding chairs stand in a circle. A woman of about twenty-two with dark curly hair in a half bun and a plain mustard sweater without logos sits in the chair facing the camera, her hand on the RIGHT side of the image frame resting on her knee and holding the sealed can by its body, its tab flat, its label toward the camera, about one metre from the camera. The can is shorter than her hand is long and keeps this size in every shot. Exactly three other people sit in the circle at the edges of the frame, turned toward her with expectant smiles: a man in a plain green t-shirt, a woman in a plain black t-shirt and a woman in a plain denim jacket, all in their early twenties. No other cup, bottle or can anywhere.
[Style and camera] Locked-off camera at the edge of the circle, 26 mm phone look, one fixed position per shot, a quarter of the frame left free above the heads; hard cut between the two shots.
[Timeline]
Shot 1 | 0-4s | Medium shot. A silent pause: she opens her mouth to speak, nothing comes, her eyes widen and drift upward blankly; the three others keep smiling, waiting. The can stays on her knee in her hand. Hard cut.
Shot 2 | 4-8s | Medium close-up of the same woman alone, in the same sweater and chair, the camera a little above her chest so the lid of the can shows. Both hands stay in frame. She takes one sip from the opening beside the tab, head tilted back a little, lowers the can to chest height, label toward the camera, and nods once, deadpan.
[Integration] Cool fluorescent light and window light from the LEFT side of the image frame fall on the can as on her sweater: a soft highlight along the metal body, a soft shadow on her fingers, the same grain and focus as her hand. The can reads as a real aluminium can, not a flat cut-out.
